program: v13 discharge of M87's registered consequences

registration_notes.N87.1: This audit may only narrow or withdraw a v13 claim, never promote one. v13 evidence is sealed and its ledger is closed.
registration_notes.N87.2: There is no 'novel' verdict. Outcomes are displaced, narrowed, unresolved. Absence of a located source is unresolved, not new.
registration_notes.N87.3: The claim list is closed at the registration commit. No claim may be added, removed, reworded or split after the first query runs.
registration_notes.N87.4: Query families are phrased to find work that would displace each claim, not work that agrees with it.
registration_notes.N87.5: Searching stops when the registered families are exhausted, not when a satisfying answer appears. Empty queries still record their counts.
registration_notes.N87.6: Title and abstract mark a source live. Only primary text with a located passage may displace or narrow.
registration_notes.N87.7: The audit measures nothing. Every v13 figure it quotes is transcribed from sealed evidence and hash-cited.
registration_notes.N87.8: This evidence is a dated snapshot and is NOT replayable. Unlike every other v13 artifact, re-running it later will return different records because the indexes change and the network is not a sealed corpus. The run records its date and the exact query strings so a reader can repeat the search, not so the bytes can be reproduced. No downstream check may treat this file as byte-reproducible.
registration_notes.N87.9: Three instrument defects were found and repaired before the audited run: arXiv exact-phrase syntax returned zero for every query including the anchors; term conjunction alone was too strict, so a fixed two-stage AND-then-OR rule now applies uniformly to every query; and Semantic Scholar rate-limiting was being recorded as emptiness, so retries were added and residual failures are recorded in failed_queries rather than counted as empty. The repaired instrument re-runs every registered query, not only the ones that returned nothing.
registration_notes.N88.1: M88's scope is closed to the three obligations M87 wrote against itself in section 7.2. No sixth claim. C2's demotion is final; a second search is not an appeal.
registration_notes.N88.2: Recall probes: named papers that certainly exist, each paired with a topic query that omits the paper's title. If a topic query aimed at a paper cannot retrieve it, 'found nothing' from the family that probe covers is not evidence of absence, and that family drops to 'not searched'.
registration_notes.N88.3: Adding an index is asymmetric. A third index can only find displacing work; it can never establish absence. A claim surviving three indexes is not better supported than one that survived two - it has merely failed to be refuted more times. No verdict may be upgraded for having searched more places.
registration_notes.N88.4: Re-running a family does not reset it. M87's verdicts stand unless this run displaces them. A re-run may move a claim down to narrowed, displaced or not-searched, and may never move one up.
registration_notes.N88.5: Reading Liznerski et al. in full may displace or narrow C1 and cannot clear it. Confirming that one paper does not anticipate a claim says nothing about the papers not read.
registration_notes.N88.6: The probe list and the reopened query families are fixed at the registration commit.
registration_notes.N88.7: Like M87, this evidence is a dated snapshot of third-party services and is NOT replayable. Re-running it will not reproduce these records.
